extracted.intended_audience: EPO search examiners acting as ISA/SISA and patent applicants under the PCT
extracted.subtask_short: PCT EPO search & written opinion guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing international search reports (ISR), written opinions (WO-ISA), and supplementary international searches (SIS/SISR) when the EPO acts as International Searching Authority or Supplementary ISA under the PCT. Covers scope, form, content, handling of unity/clarity/priority issues, citation practices, transmittal and public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, an opinion must be given on all searched claims. Only one independent claim in each category needs to be treated in detail; short comments would normally suffice for further independent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple independent claims in one category are per se not a reason for an incomplete search. For additional independent claims brief comments are normally sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of search for clarity problems
rubrics_metrics.description: If the complexity lies in lack of clarity, the search will be restricted first, and the non-unity objection applied to the clear parts of the claimed subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invitation to pay additional fees may remark on clarity problems related to further inventions. The EPO as ISA may ask the applicant to clarify the subject-matter to be searched using the procedure in GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.3–3.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of limitations of scope of the search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible limitations include: (i) a declaration issued instead of the search report (Art.17(2)(a)); (ii) an incomplete search report (Art.17(2)(b)); (iii) a partial international search report due to lack of unity (Art.17(3)(a) and Rule 13); (iv) an incomplete search report due to missing sequence listings (GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISR must indicate whether the subject of the search was restricted and which claims have or have not been searched. The reasons for no search should be indicated in the declaration. In some cases the extent/reasons for restriction may be indicated only in the WO-ISA rather than the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions of the international search report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A search report must contain no matter, in particular no expressions of opinion, reasoning, arguments or explanations, other than that required by the Form or referred to in GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 9.2.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not apply to the written opinion; the ISR should avoid additional commentary beyond prescribed form items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of search strategy information sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Search reports drawn up by the EPO are supplemented with an "Information on Search Strategy" sheet listing the databases searched, classification symbols defining the extent of the search, and the keywords or other retrieval elements used by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sheet is automatically generated from examiner inputs and (during the pilot) may change content. Upon publication the sheet will be available to the public via PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO as ISA classifies the application according to the IPC and CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification data must be prepared and recorded in the search report; see related EPO guidelines for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract, title and figure publication data
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A1 publication the examiner indicates on supplemental sheet A the approval or amendment of the abstract (which should not exceed 150 words), the approval or amendment of the title, and the figure to accompany the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is to be published before the ISR is prepared (A2 publication), titles, abstracts and figures are published as submitted by the applicant. First filings cannot be published as A2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating restriction of the subject of the search in the ISR/SO
rubrics_metrics.description: When the search is restricted (e.g., lack of unity, claims where no meaningful search possible, missing sequence listings), the ISR, declaration, or incomplete/partial search report must indicate whether the subject of the search was restricted and which claims were searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cases where meaningful search was impossible a declaration instead of a search report should indicate reasons. Where partial/incomplete searches occur, the extent and reasons may be indicated in the WO-ISA rather than the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and bibliographic elements of cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the search report must be identified with appropriate bibliographic elements and corresponding document relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the EPO Guidelines (B-X, 9.1.1 and 9.1.2) mutatis mutandis; include languages of documents and authentication/date checks where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and indication of document categories (X, Y, P, A, D, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents in the search report must be categorized (X, Y, P, A, D, etc.) according to their relevance and role in assessing novelty/inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly relevant documents (X/Y) should be identified; P documents (priority documents) and non-patent literature should be indicated even if not used for further examination; see GL/ISPE references for category guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of "P" documents
rubrics_metrics.description: "P" documents are to be indicated in the search report even though they are normally not used for further examination; if the priority document is not available it is assumed valid for establishing the search report and written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority document is later available and the priority found invalid, the examiner must provide detailed comments since such documents then become prior art under Rule 33.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between cited documents and claims; identification of relevant passages
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report and accompanying documentation should set out the relationship between documents cited and the claims, and identify the relevant passages in prior art documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear mapping from cited documents to specific claims and specify the passages relied upon (see GL/ISPE references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication and dates of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication and dating of cited documents must be handled according to the Examination Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify dates and authenticity of documents as necessary; follow Rule 43.2, 43.8 and GL/ISPE references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies attached to the search report and use of "&" sign
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of the ISR is sent to the IB and one to the applicant; the applicant copy is accompanied by copies of all documents cited except those appearing after the "&" symbol which are not designated for copying and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the transmission rules in GL/EPO B-X and Rule 44 series; electronic copies and family member handling are specified in related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of search report and written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO forwards one copy of the search report (or declaration) and the written opinion to the IB and one copy to the applicant. Applicants also receive copies of cited documents and, when appropriate, automated translations annexed to the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper annexing of translations and designated copies; follow Rule 44 and GL/ISPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the written opinion (WO-ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The WO-ISA gives a preliminary and non-binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step and to be industrially applicable. When appropriate, it also addresses added subject-matter, unity, insufficient disclosure and clarity or support issues, as well as formal defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings must be consistent with document categories in the search report and with other issues raised (e.g., lack of unity or limitation of the search). If there are no defects the WO-ISA should state reasons why the application is considered to fulfil the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the written opinion (documents considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The WO-ISA relates to the application documents as originally filed (or a translation thereof); replies to informal clarifications are taken into account when drawing up the written opinion. Replacement pages filed under Rule 26 or Rule 91.1 are deemed part of the application "as originally filed".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must check any later-filed parts (e.g., furnished under Rule 20) for the "completely contained" criterion and consider how such filings affect the WO-ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned objections for novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A full explanation of the conclusions reached should always be given for all searched claims, regardless of whether the conclusion is positive or negative. The opinion given in the WO-ISA is restricted to what has actually been searched and this should be made clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally only one independent claim in each category is treated in detail; for negative conclusions regarding further independent claims and dependent claims comments may be shorter, but full explanation should be given for searched claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims in the WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims should be indicated as complying or not with the requirements of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability. Short statements of the reasons why the claims do not comply should be given on the separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the examiner's discretion, more detailed comments may be made about selected dependent claims. If any claims are found to be novel and inventive, brief reasons for this should be given on the separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, conciseness, support and formal defects reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Major clarity, conciseness or support issues will be mentioned under Box VIII unless they make a meaningful search impossible (in which case treated under Section III). Formal defects and minor clarity issues are dealt with under Boxes VII and VIII respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is severely deficient and claims will need drastic redrafting, it is not necessary to make objections about minor clarity or formal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making suggestions in the WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to make suggestions in the written opinion as to how certain objections may be overcome, but the examiner must not make any final amendments to the application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WO-ISA should not give the impression that compliance with suggestions would lead to an allowable application under the EPC or any national law, nor should it suggest the applicant actively file submissions (since WO-ISA may convert to IPRP Chapter I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking the WO-ISA positive or negative
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner needs to indicate whether the WO-ISA is to be considered positive or negative for further prosecution. A WO-ISA is considered positive if it contains no objections at all or only minor objections which would not hinder a direct grant in the EP phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: where P/E documents cited but priority could not be checked and there are no other objections, WO-ISA is considered positive; if non-unitary and all inventions searched were novel and inventive but lack unity is the only objection, WO-ISA is marked negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of priority claims in WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority need only be checked normally if a relevant P or E document is found during the search. If the priority document is not available, the opinion will be established on the assumption that the claimed priority is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority is checked and found invalid, indicate this under Section II and provide detailed comments for documents that become prior art; restoration of priority should be referenced per GL/PCT-EPO guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'E' documents in the written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: E documents (potential Art.54(3) EPC documents) will be mentioned under Section VI if they are considered prejudicial to the novelty of at least one claim. If relevance is independent of priority being valid or priority checked and invalid, give reasons for the novelty objection and indicate relevance in the European phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document would only be relevant under Art.54(3) EPC if priority is invalid and the priority could not be checked, no reasons need to be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: WO-ISA in relation to lack of unity and restricted searches
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of lack of unity where more than one invention has been searched, for each invention searched one independent claim in each category must be treated in detail. When the search was restricted, the WO-ISA opinion is normally restricted to what has actually been searched and must be consistent with the restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO B-VII and B-VIII for further detail on unity and restriction handling; arguments and objections must align with the declared scope of the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing omissions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant has not filed an electronic sequence listing conforming to WIPO Standard ST.25 or has not paid late furnishing fee, the WO-ISA will indicate that the written opinion is limited to the same extent as the search (Rule 5.2; Rule 13ter.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WO-ISA should indicate limitation under Section III and reference the relevant rules and OJ EPO guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary International Search (SIS) purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: SIS is optional for applicants and International Authorities to obtain further supplementary searches from other Authorities during the international phase; the EPO as SISA accepts a limited number of SIS requests per year (since 2010 limited to 700 per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request SIS up to the end of 22 months from the priority date; SISR must be established within 28 months from the priority date to be useful for regional/national phase decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and scope of the Supplementary International Search (SIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIS is always made on the claims as originally filed (or a translation) and at the EPO the scope of a SIS is the same as for any other international search carried out by the EPO and is not limited to documentation in a specific language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the main ISA ISR is available it will be taken into account; the SISA will not automatically adopt limitations made by the main ISA but will assess appropriateness case-by-case under EPO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling out the supplementary international search report (SISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SISR is filled out similarly to any international search report, except publication details need not be provided as the main ISA already provided publication data and IPC classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will not cite in the SISR a document already cited in the ISR unless a different significance is attached; the SISR should indicate whether the main ISR was available and taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations (Scope Annex) for SIS instead of separate WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: No separate WO-ISA is established for a SIS. A free-text sheet (Scope Annex) containing the same information as the WO-ISA explanations is used, and a positive conclusion must be reasoned as in a WO-ISA/IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scope Annex concentrates on documents cited in the SISR but may raise objections based on documents cited in the ISR; it should avoid unnecessary re-evaluation of WO-ISA objections from the main ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of documents cited in both ISR and SISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will not cite in the SISR a document already cited in the ISR unless a different significance is attached to it (e.g., as a Y document in combination or if the main ISR clearly failed to recognise relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner disagrees with categories assigned in the ISR and wishes to base objections on those documents, the documents will be cited again in the SISR; A documents found by the EPO as SISA will be cited in the SISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of priority and treatment of E/P documents in SISR
rubrics_metrics.description: At SIS stage the priority document should be in the file and can be checked; if not available, priority is assumed valid for search purposes. If priority is not valid, this will be explained in the Scope Annex and P documents dealt with in detail. Any E document potentially Art.54(3) EPC will be addressed in the Scope Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be made aware of E documents' relevance if entering the European phase; reasoning and implications for national/regional phases should be given where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of documents cited in the SISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant will receive a copy of each document cited in the SISR free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 45bis provisions and GL/ISPE references regarding transmittal and free copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-unity procedure for SIS
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of non-unity only one invention is searched in SIS; there is no possibility to pay additional fees for further inventions. Where the main ISA objected to lack of unity, the applicant can indicate with the SIS request which invention should be searched by the SISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision as to which invention is the main one and to be searched is handled differently for SIS and detailed rules are in GL/PCT-EPO B-XII, 10.2–10.3.
